cells.tense: You are standing inside something you helped make, and you know it.
cells.ask: Show one piece of what you've made to someone who wasn't there for it, and let their seeing it complete the picture.
cells.core:
You're in the middle of something you helped make, and it's working. The meals, the rituals, the way your people say a thing — some of it came through you, and you can feel that. Not because you're holding it up, but because you can see the shape it took and you're glad.

The hard part isn't getting here. It's letting the thing be finished in someone else's hands. When your part is done, it keeps going on its own; you can watch it go and still be part of it. Your next move is small: show one piece to someone who hasn't seen it, and see what they do with it.

cells.verb: Feeling the full weight of what was imagined into a shared thing
cells.place: In the shared meaning that gets carried between people

cells.tense: You are already living in a version of this that hasn't arrived yet, and you are pulling the people around you toward it.
cells.ask: Choose one piece you're tending and leave it untouched for a week; at the end, name what grew while you let it alone.
cells.core:
You're living in the finished version and the people around you aren't. You can see what this practice, this tradition, this thing you're building is supposed to become — so you're pushing the shape you see before the present one has had room. The pushing is eating the satisfaction you set out to build.

What's available instead is a slower tending. You're not the only one who has to hold this up; you can watch it grow without your hand on it. Pick one piece and step back from it for a week. The parts that stay standing are the parts that didn't need your grip.

cells.tense: You stepped back from the shared thing once and you have stayed where you stopped.
cells.ask: Say the first thing you actually think about one shared thing you've kept quiet on, out loud, before you edit it.
cells.core:
In its own shape, this is handing something over without ceremony. You say the thing, you pass it forward, and you don't stand around checking whether it landed. The offer is made and the rest is theirs. It takes almost nothing out of you.

That offer isn't happening now. You still know what's worth keeping — you just don't say it, don't put it forward, so the shared things get built by other people while you watch from a step back. Start with something small and unpolished. Say one true thing you've been holding back, before you've decided whether it's the right thing to say.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what your people carry forward, and you describe it as something that just happened.
cells.ask: Pick one practice your people have picked up, and say out loud, once, that it came through you.
cells.core:
At its plainest, this is ordinary: you make something, it gets picked up, and the hands that shaped it are known. No ceremony needed. The credit travels with the thing and nobody has to argue about where it came from.

That part isn't happening. You're already a hand in what your people carry — how you put things, what you keep doing when nobody's watching — but when it comes up, the story is that the group does it, or it's just how things are here, or someone else started it. One thing is enough. Choose a practice your people have taken up, and say plainly that it traveled through you. The thing itself doesn't change. Your place in it does.

attempts.check: The record names the parent as Imagination, and the kernel says the card is 'Abundant vision realized,' but it does not establish that this person has actually imagined anything; the reading can only speak to a capacity for satisfaction in what has been made, not to its content. A reader could reasonably say the card's picture is about a private inner state, not about shared life, so the cells must stay close to what is actually transmitted between people. Too Much and Too Little are written as opposite failures of receiving and passing on what has been made. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be any that calls satisfaction a duty; it is cut.
